title: Microsoft-proposed Ratepayer Protection Tariff for large loads in NV Energy territory
utility: Nevada Power Company / Sierra Pacific Power Company (NV Energy)

latestAction.text: Utility Dive reported Microsoft's May 2026 filing of a proposed Ratepayer Protection Tariff in PUCN Docket 20-08014; commission evaluation and public comment ongoing.

summary: In May 2026 Microsoft filed a proposed Ratepayer Protection Tariff in PUCN Docket 20-08014, an investigatory docket opened in August 2020 after heat-wave capacity shortfalls. The proposal splits the cost of project-specific substations, generation and transmission into a Customer Contributed Share, paid by the large-load customer upfront or through facility payments, and a System Benefit Share that could enter rate base if it benefits the wider system. It also includes customer-specific asset tracking, electric service agreements with contract demand, load ramps and exit charges, a 'Bring Your Own Power' option, and 60-day expedited approval for projects the developer fully funds upfront.
significance: This is a hyperscaler-authored template for how Nevada might make data centers pay for the grid build-out they trigger. NV Energy reports roughly 22 GW of large-load interest against an ~8.5 GW system peak, so whatever cost-allocation rule the PUCN adopts will shape speed-to-power and ratepayer exposure for every new campus.

caveats: Exact May 2026 filing date not confirmed, and the PUCN docket page was not reachable. A secondary source reported hearings in January 2027 and a decision by mid-2027, but that is unverified and omitted.

title: MISO Expedited Resource Addition Study (ERAS)

latestAction.text: Sierra Club and other public interest organizations petitioned for court review after FERC denied rehearing by operation of law (September 22, 2025); further FERC consideration of rehearing (ER25-2454-002) pending.

summary: After FERC rejected its first proposal in May 2025 (ER25-1674) for lacking a cap on participating projects, MISO refiled ERAS on June 6, 2025. FERC accepted it on July 21, 2025, subject to condition (192 FERC ¶ 61,064). ERAS is a temporary fast-track interconnection study for generation tied to a specific load addition or resource-adequacy deficiency, with service capped at 150% of identified need within the same Local Resource Zone and a limit of 68 projects (including IPP and retail-choice carve-outs). A September 4, 2025 letter order accepted compliance revisions. In ER25-3543 MISO later proposed raising the quarterly study cap from 10 to 15 projects.
significance: ERAS is how MISO utilities such as Entergy, Ameren and Xcel get gas and other generation for data-center loads connected ahead of the backlogged regular queue. It speeds up supply for hyperscale campuses in Louisiana, Mississippi, Indiana and elsewhere, and environmental groups argue it is unduly preferential.

title: PGE large-load investigation and POWER Act (HB 3546) Schedule 96 data-center rate class

latestAction.text: OPUC approved Schedule 96, a new large-load rate class for PGE, and contract requirements for future PGE data-center agreements (Order No. 26-154).

summary: OPUC opened UM 2377 to examine large-load impacts raised in PGE rate cases. HB 3546 (2025, the POWER Act) then required a separate tariff class for facilities of 20 MW or more on contracts of at least 10 years. In May 2026 the commission created Schedule 96 for large data centers and other large loads. It requires minimum-term contracts with predictable charges if a customer does not use the infrastructure PGE built, requires sufficient clean energy resources before a large customer takes service, and makes data centers pay for the emissions-free power needed to serve them. A 1-cent/kWh surcharge on Schedule 96 customers with 100 MW or more of allocated capacity funds programs that offset residential and low-income costs.
significance: This is the first full implementation of Oregon's POWER Act, which was among the first state laws to require a separate data-center rate class. It governs the Hillsboro data-center cluster in PGE territory and is a model other states cite for keeping data-center costs off household bills.

title: OG&E proposed Large Load Tariff (75 MW+) under the Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026

latestAction.text: OCC granted motion for procedural schedule; commissioners set November 3, 2026 as the decision date.

summary: OG&E filed a large-load tariff for new customers expecting at least 75 MW, existing customers adding 75 MW of incremental demand or exceeding 125 MW, and customers whose load profile changes to meet the threshold. Covered customers would be billed on contracted demand whether or not they use it, would pay 100% of grid-connection costs upfront, and would pay a monthly charge estimated at $25-30 million a year that funds future credits for residential and financially vulnerable customers, subject to review in a rate case. The filing follows Oklahoma's Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026 (17 O.S. 900-906, 75 MW threshold, effective July 1, 2026).
significance: This is Oklahoma's first generic data-center tariff and puts the new state ratepayer-protection law into practice. Its monthly residential-credit charge is unusual. The decision is due on Election Day 2026, which makes it politically salient.

title: Entergy Mississippi recovery of Amazon data-center-driven investments (SB 2001 framework and formula rate plan)

latestAction.text: Entergy said the PSC-approved 2026 annual formula rate plan avoided a $4.87/month increase because of data-center revenue; a further $0.41 reduction filing was pending for October.

summary: Under 2024's SB 2001, Entergy Mississippi's grid and generation investments for Amazon's central-Mississippi data centers (about $25 billion of planned investment) can proceed without standard PSC certification. They are deemed 'used and useful', subject only to after-the-fact prudence review, and the PSC cannot modify the Amazon contract during its term. Entergy is building three combined-cycle gas plants (Greenville, Vicksburg, Ridgeland) totaling more than 2,100 MW. A May 2026 Synapse/Earthjustice report estimated the projects have already raised residential bills by about $10.60/month, which Entergy disputes, saying data-center revenue held 2026 formula-rate-plan rates flat.
significance: Mississippi shows the minimal-oversight model: the commission's main lever is prudence review in formula rate plan filings, and the contract terms are confidential. The disputed bill impacts are an affordability flashpoint in a state with elected commissioners.

title: Delmarva Power large-load tariff and pause on new large-load interconnections

latestAction.text: Deadline for Delmarva's final tariff version after public comments closed April 6; joint Staff/DNREC/DPA comments urged a more deliberate approach. Hearing examiner findings were expected in summer 2026.

summary: After a petition presented on September 3, 2025 (backed by Governor Meyer and the Public Advocate), the PSC opened Docket 25-0826 and paused interconnection of new 25 MW+ loads in Delmarva territory until a large-load tariff is in place. Delmarva filed its proposed tariff on December 19, 2025, covering customers with peak demand of 25 MW or more, though it has suggested raising the threshold to 50 MW. PSC Staff, DNREC and the Division of the Public Advocate jointly raised serious concerns about customer risk and asked that the tariff align with PJM and federal developments. DNREC questioned the assumptions behind roughly 2,455 MW of proposed new demand, including the 1,200 MW Project Washington data center in Delaware City.
significance: Delaware is one of the few states with an outright moratorium on new large-load hookups until tariff protections exist. A 1,200 MW campus would be close to half the state's ~2,700 MW summer peak, so the tariff decides whether hyperscale development can proceed in Delaware at all.

title: NY PSC proceeding on interconnection reform and cost responsibility for large loads (Energize NY Development)

latestAction.text: Reply comments due on the Order Instituting Proceeding; a technical conference is required before Dec. 31, 2026 and a Staff white paper before Feb. 12, 2027.

summary: The PSC instituted the proceeding at its February 12, 2026 session under Governor Hochul's Energize NY Development initiative. Its objectives are to modernize large-load interconnection, improve transparency on grid upgrades and costs, make large loads bear the system costs they impose, keep the grid reliable, align with the CLCPA, and test whether large loads can push rates down. The PSC will develop criteria to define and categorize large loads, treating data centers and crypto mining differently, and is considering impact-based cost recovery, customer-supplied generation or storage, curtailment and flexibility obligations, long-term contracts and tariff revisions. Initial and reply comments were due April 13 and May 13, 2026.
significance: This is New York's main venue for data-center cost allocation and interconnection rules. It is running alongside Executive Order No. 62 (July 2026), which pauses discretionary DEC permits for data centers pending a DPS generic environmental review, and the legislature's Responsible Data Center Development Act. Together these put New York among the most restrictive states for new large data centers.

title: Alabama PSC review process for Alabama Power large-load data-center contracts (Act 2026-610)

latestAction.text: PSC unanimously adopted final review procedures: commission vote within 90 days of each petition or the contract is deemed approved; public summary plus confidential filing with PSC staff and the Attorney General.

summary: Act 2026-610 (SB 270, effective October 1, 2026) requires the PSC to find that Alabama Power's data-center contracts are expected to recover incremental costs and benefit other retail customers. The PSC opened Docket 33709 to set the review process and took comments in August 2026. The final procedures require a public petition naming the customer and its parent, the location, and the maximum contracted capacity. The full contract and a Rate Impact Measure analysis go only to PSC staff and the AG. The commission must vote within 90 days or the contract is deemed approved, and there is no public hearing or intervention. Contracts filed before October 1 under interim rules include Dotier LLC (Meta, June 18), Alabama ADC Holdings (Nebius, July 24) and Woostor LLC (August 14).
significance: Proposed data-center load in Alabama could exceed all residential use, and Alabama Power has delayed until 2028 recovery of a $622 million gas plant bought largely for that demand. The confidential contract-by-contract model with deemed approval is a major affordability issue, criticized by Energy Alabama, SELC and the AG's office, in a state with elected PSC members.

Cheyenne Light's separate 2026 IRP (20003-275-EA-26) excludes capacity for individually contracted LPCS customers.
significance: Wyoming's data-center model has large customers self-supply or contract for dedicated resources under LPCS. Proposed campuses (2.7 GW at Project Jade) are several times the state's load, so how transmission upgrades for them are allocated decides whether Cheyenne-area residential customers are protected.

title: Mon Power / Potomac Edison certificate for 1,200 MW Maidsville (Fort Martin) combined-cycle gas plant and 70 MW solar

latestAction.text: PSC evidentiary hearing began; Mon Power's president testified that data-center contracts would credit customers for surcharges paid. A PSC decision is expected by March 2027.

summary: In early 2026 Mon Power and Potomac Edison applied for consent and a certificate of convenience and necessity for a ~1,200 MW combined-cycle plant at Fort Martin/Maidsville in Monongalia County (about $2.48 billion) plus 70 MW of solar at three sites ($182 million). Costs would be recovered through a customer surcharge, with operation targeted by end of 2031. The companies cite load growth 'especially data center growth' and say they are in talks with three data-center developers whose contracts would reimburse customers' surcharge payments. Advocates want conditions or a large-load tariff so data centers pay their share. FirstEnergy prefers individual special contracts.
significance: This is West Virginia's main data-center-driven generation case. Residential customers would pay surcharges for a plant justified by data-center load that is not yet contracted, and the state has no large-load tariff to backstop them. It tests the state's pro-data-center policy (HB 2014 microgrids) against affordability concerns.

title: Otter Tail Power petition for a new very-large-customer class and High Power Compute rate schedule
summary: Otter Tail Power asks the SD PUC to split its Large General Service class into tiers and create a new class for very large customers (25 MW or more). The petition replaces the Super Large General Service schedule with a Tier II schedule and creates Section 10.07, a Large General Service Tier III High Power Compute schedule for customers above a firm-load threshold. Otter Tail says the goal is to apply tariff provisions consistently across its jurisdictions and protect non-participating customers from costs tied to very large loads. It cites unprecedented demand from data-center developers. The filing follows South Dakota's SB 135 'Data Center Bill of Rights for Citizens' (effective July 1, 2026), which sets requirements for large-load tariffs. Proposed effective date is January 1, 2027.
significance: This is the first South Dakota large-load and data-center tariff filed after SB 135. It will set the template other SD utilities (Xcel, Black Hills, NorthWestern) are likely to follow for allocating costs to hyperscale and AI campuses.

summary: The ND PSC approved MDU's amended service agreement with Applied Digital's high-density compute campus, raising service from 225 MW to 350 MW and extending the term to August 31, 2030. Service runs under MDU's Rate 45 High Density Contracted Demand Response tariff (Case PU-22-337, approved 2023), which is ND's main mechanism for very large data-center load. MDU reportedly has a pending general rate increase alongside further data-center service requests.
significance: Rate 45 and the Applied Digital contract are North Dakota's working model for serving AI and crypto loads with curtailable, contracted demand. The PSC has two of three seats on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

latestAction.text: DPU issued a directive to Unitil, Eversource and National Grid on handling data-center interconnection requests.

summary: The Massachusetts DPU issued a directive under Executive Order 658 instructing the three investor-owned distribution companies to take specified actions on data-center interconnection requests. Massachusetts has no dedicated large-load tariff, and large-load service is handled through general rate cases. The House version of the 2026 energy affordability bill would have required a data-center-specific tariff.
significance: This is the DPU's first formal step on data-center load and may lead to a large-load tariff requirement in Massachusetts, where affordability legislation is pending.
